problem: The plotted points do not form the two straight lines the caption and text promise. From 0 to 20 mL the fall is 1 unit per mL (40 → 30 → 20), but from 20 to 25 mL it falls 2 units per mL (20 → 10). After the minimum the rise is 2 units per mL (10 → 20) and then 1 unit per mL (20 → 30). A student sees a bent curve, not a V of straight lines meeting at 25.0 mL, and the intersection/slope reading being taught is contradicted by the picture.
fix: Use points on two straight branches, e.g. [[0, 40], [10, 28], [20, 16], [25, 10], [30, 15], [40, 25]]: a straight fall of slope −1.2 per mL up to the minimum at 25.0 mL, then a straight rise of slope +1 per mL. Keep the same axis limits and aria text.

problem: The bullet mixes two different mistakes. Using concentration in mol m⁻³ really does give a 1000-fold error (1 mol m⁻³ = 0.001 mol L⁻¹, so the answer comes out 1000 times too small). Substituting resistance R for κ is simply the wrong quantity, not a 1000-fold error, so the sentence misleads.
fix: In Λm = 1000κ/M, κ must be in S cm⁻¹ and M in mol L⁻¹; a concentration given in mol m⁻³ makes the answer 1000 times too small, and R must first be converted to κ = (l/A)/R.
